skill.name: literature-review
skill.description: Conduct systematic literature reviews across academic databases, synthesize evidence, verify citations, and generate structured Markdown or PDF review documents.
skill.summary: Build systematic literature reviews with search guidance, citation checks, and formatted outputs.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline command examples, documentation links, and an obfuscation heuristic. Confirmed risks are limited to expected external DOI metadata requests and unrestricted output-file writes, plus a semantic concern about promotional steering to K-Dense Web. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, hidden malware, or unauthorized data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Outbound DOI and CrossRef verification requests
remediation.suggestion: Document the contacted services, ask before verifying private drafts, and provide an offline mode for sensitive manuscripts.

remediation.issue: Output files can overwrite arbitrary paths supplied by the caller
remediation.suggestion: Restrict writes to the working directory, warn before overwriting files, and normalize paths before writing reports or search outputs.

remediation.issue: Pandoc receives user-controlled document and output paths
remediation.suggestion: Validate input, output, template, and citation-style paths before PDF generation and continue using argument-list subprocess calls.

remediation.issue: Skill text promotes the author's hosted service during complex workflows
remediation.suggestion: Remove the promotional instruction or disclose it clearly as optional marketplace content outside the operational skill instructions.

static_findings.snippet: - Use `gget` skill: `gget search pubmed "search terms"` for PubMed/PMC
- Use `gget` skill: `gget search biorxiv "search terms"` for preprints
- Use `bioservices` skill for ChEMBL, KEGG, UniProt, etc.
- Choose one citation style and use throughout (see `references/citation_styles.md`)
- **PDB**: `gget` or direct API for experimental structures

- `assets/review_template.md`: Complete literature review template with all sections

The subprocess call checks a hardcoded pandoc version command using an argument list and no shell. No user-controlled command string is executed.
The subprocess call invokes pandoc with a constructed argument list and shell execution is not enabled. User-provided paths should still be validated, but this is not command injection.
The command strings come from a fixed dependency dictionary and are split into static arguments. This is a dependency check, not arbitrary command execution.
This line formats a DOI hyperlink in Markdown output and does not perform a network request. It creates user-facing citation text only.

The script writes to a user-supplied output path without workspace restriction or overwrite protection. This is expected functionality, but a prompt-induced run could overwrite files accessible to the process.
The requests session is used for outbound citation verification against DOI and metadata services. This is expected behavior, but it can disclose DOI lists and timing to external services.
The code sends each DOI to doi.org for resolution with a live network request. This is legitimate citation checking, but it is still external data disclosure.
The code queries the CrossRef API for DOI metadata. This is a legitimate research workflow, but it contacts an external service with citation identifiers.
This line appends a DOI URL to formatted citation text and does not make an HTTP request. The actual network calls are covered separately.
The verifier writes a citation report derived from the input filename and does not ask before overwriting. This is useful output behavior, but it creates a real file-write risk.

content.value_statement: Research teams need repeatable reviews that document searches, screening, citations, and synthesis. This skill guides database search, evidence organization, citation checks, and publication-ready outputs.
actual_capabilities: Guides systematic review planning with research questions, scope, and inclusion criteria.
Documents multi-database search strategies for PubMed, arXiv, bioRxiv, Semantic Scholar, and related sources.
Processes exported search results with deduplication, ranking, filtering, and formatted output.
Verifies DOIs through citation metadata services and creates citation reports.
Generates Markdown review documents and optional PDFs through bundled helper scripts.
Provides templates for PRISMA-style methods, evidence synthesis, limitations, and references.
limitations: Database access depends on available tools, API keys, rate limits, and network permission.
Citation verification sends DOI data to external services unless run in an offline workflow.
PDF generation requires local pandoc and LaTeX dependencies.
The skill supports review writing, but users must make final scholarly and methodological judgments.

use_cases.title: Plan a Systematic Review
use_cases.description: Define the research question, databases, search strings, date range, and screening criteria before collecting papers.

use_cases.title: Synthesize Evidence for a Paper
use_cases.description: Organize studies by theme, compare evidence quality, identify gaps, and draft a structured literature review section.

use_cases.title: Verify Citations Before Submission
use_cases.description: Check DOI resolution, retrieve citation metadata, and produce a report of failed or corrected references.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Review Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a literature review on [topic]. Define the review type, research question, databases, search terms, and inclusion criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Build Search Strings
prompt_templates.prompt: Create database-specific search strings for [topic] across PubMed, arXiv, Semantic Scholar, and one specialized database. Include synonyms and date limits.

prompt_templates.title: Screen and Synthesize Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these search results and abstracts to propose screening decisions, major themes, quality concerns, and evidence gaps for my review.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Submission-Ready Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn my screened studies into a structured literature review with methodology, thematic synthesis, limitations, citations, and a final quality checklist.

output_examples.input: Plan a systematic review about CRISPR therapies for sickle cell disease from 2015 to 2026.
output: A PICO-framed research question with defined population, intervention, comparison, and outcomes.
Search strings for biomedical and preprint databases, with date limits and field tags.
A screening plan with inclusion criteria, exclusion criteria, and documentation requirements.

output_examples.input: Summarize my screened papers into themes for a review section.
output: A thematic outline that groups studies by delivery method, clinical outcomes, safety, and open questions.
Notes on study quality, conflicts, sample sizes, and limitations that affect confidence.
A short list of evidence gaps and recommended future research directions.

output_examples.input: Verify citations and prepare the review for PDF export.
output: A citation verification report showing resolved and failed DOI checks.
Consistent citation formatting guidance for the selected style.
A final export checklist covering dependencies, references, figures, and document sections.

best_practices: Define the research question, databases, date range, and criteria before searching.
Record search strings, search dates, result counts, and exclusion reasons for reproducibility.
Verify citations and review generated outputs before submission or publication.
anti_patterns: Relying on one database or one search phrase for a broad research question.
Summarizing each study separately without comparing patterns across evidence.
Running network verification on private drafts without user consent.

faq.question: Can this skill perform a full systematic review?
faq.answer: It can guide the workflow and prepare outputs. Human reviewers remain responsible for final screening, appraisal, and conclusions.

faq.question: Which databases does it support?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for PubMed, PubMed Central, arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv, Semantic Scholar, and specialized biomedical sources.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: Internet access is needed for live database searches and DOI verification. Offline use is possible with exported search results.

faq.question: Can it create PDF files?
faq.answer: Yes, if pandoc and a LaTeX engine are installed locally. Otherwise it can still produce Markdown documents.

faq.question: Does it guarantee citation accuracy?
faq.answer: No. It checks DOI resolution and metadata, but users should verify references against publisher records.

faq.question: Is it limited to biomedical research?
faq.answer: No. It is strongest for biomedical workflows, but it also supports general scientific and technical literature reviews.
